title: Real conversations
goal: Hold long, natural conversations: catch up with an old friend, sit through a family dinner talking to grandparents, aunts and cousins in the right register, argue about where to go, and plan a trip together.
intro:
This last unit puts everything together. Real conversations are long, messy and full of people: you catch up with a college friend you haven't seen in years, then go to a festival dinner where you talk to your grandmother, an aunt and a younger cousin in the same breath, and end up arguing about whether the weekend trip should be Kodagu or Gokarna.

Two skills make this possible. The first is **linking**: instead of short sentences joined with 'and then', fluent Kannada builds one long sentence from participles and endings (ಎದ್ದು, ಸ್ನಾನ ಮಾಡಿ, ತಿಂಡಿ ತಿಂದು ಹೊರಟೆ) and saves the only full verb for the end. The second is **switching register** on the fly: ನೀವು and ಬನ್ನಿ for Ajji, ನೀನು and ಬಾ for your cousin, ಬನ್ರೋ for the whole gang. Get those right and you're having real conversations in Kannada.

vocab.note: ನಮ್ಮ ಬ್ಯಾಚ್ 'our batch'; ಬ್ಯಾಚ್‌ಮೇಟ್ 'classmate'.
Usually organised on a WhatsApp group that never stops pinging.
Intransitive: ನೀನು ಬದಲಾಗಿದ್ದೀಯ 'you've changed'. To change something is ಬದಲಾಯಿಸು (unit 17).
Lit. 'talk and story'. Also formal 'negotiations'.
ಸರ್ಪ್ರೈಸ್ ಕೊಡು 'to surprise (someone)'. Kannada ಅಚ್ಚರಿ / ಆಶ್ಚರ್ಯ.
Granddaughter: ಮೊಮ್ಮಗಳು; grandchildren: ಮೊಮ್ಮಕ್ಕಳು.
Treated as an honoured guest: ಅಳಿಯಂದಿರು is the respectful form. Daughter-in-law is ಸೊಸೆ.
ಎಲ್ಲಾ ಕ್ಷೇಮನಾ? 'is everyone well?', the traditional greeting between elders and on the phone to relatives. Answer: ಎಲ್ಲಾ ಕ್ಷೇಮ.
Lit. 'big people'. ದೊಡ್ಡವರ ಮುಂದೆ 'in front of the elders'. Sarcastic: ನೀವೇ ದೊಡ್ಡವರು 'you're the boss'.
Joins two sentences: ತಡ ಆಯ್ತು, ಹಾಗಾಗಿ ಬರಲಿಲ್ಲ. More formal: ಆದ್ದರಿಂದ.
From ಇಲ್ಲ ಅಂದರೆ 'if not'. Also ಇಲ್ಲದಿದ್ರೆ. ಬೇಗ ಬಾ, ಇಲ್ಲಾಂದ್ರೆ ಬಿಟ್ಟು ಹೋಗ್ತೀವಿ 'come quickly, or we'll leave without you'.

vocab.en: to get along, fit in, adjust
vocab.note: ಅವರ ಜೊತೆ ಹೊಂದಿಕೊಳ್ಳೋದು ಕಷ್ಟ 'it's hard to get along with them'. In speech often just ಅಡ್ಜಸ್ಟ್ ಮಾಡ್ಕೊಳ್ಳು.

vocab.en: to sulk, be in a huff
vocab.note: Spoken ಮುನಿಸ್ಕೊಂಡಿದ್ದಾಳೆ 'she's sulking', ಮುನಿಸ್ಕೋಬೇಡ 'don't sulk'. The noun is ಮುನಿಸು.
ವೋಟ್ ಮಾಡು 'to vote'. In elections also ಮತ, ಮತ ಹಾಕು.
ರಾಜಿ ಆಗು 'to compromise, make up'; ರಾಜಿ ಮಾಡಿಸು 'to broker a settlement'.
ನನ್ನ ಸರದಿ 'my turn'; ಸರದಿ ಸಾಲು 'a queue'.
ಬಜೆಟ್ ಒಳಗೆ 'within budget'.
ಖರ್ಚು ಮಾಡು 'to spend'; ಖರ್ಚು ಎಷ್ಟಾಯ್ತು? 'how much did it cost?'
The classic way to stay in Kodagu and Chikkamagaluru: a family home on a coffee estate, with home-cooked food.
The winding roads down the Western Ghats to the coast: Charmadi, Shiradi, Agumbe.
Karnataka's most famous is ಜೋಗ ಜಲಪಾತ (Jog Falls). Casually also ಫಾಲ್ಸ್.
Sunset: ಸೂರ್ಯಾಸ್ತ.

phrases.en: It's been ages since I saw you! (informal)
phrases.note: Polite: ಎಷ್ಟು ದಿನ ಆಯ್ತು ನಿಮ್ಮನ್ನ ನೋಡಿ!
What elders and relatives ask; the answer is ಎಲ್ಲಾ ಕ್ಷೇಮ, ನಿಮ್ಮ ಆಶೀರ್ವಾದ 'all well, thanks to your blessings'.

phrases.en: Shall I serve you another one?
phrases.note: Hosts ask this two or three times; say ಸಾಕು firmly if you mean it.

phrases.en: So be it. / Let's do that.

grammar.title: Linking long sentences: -ಇ chains, -ತಾ, -ಓದ್ರಿಂದ, -ಲಿ ಅಂತ, -ಅದೆ
grammar.body:
Fluent speakers don't string short sentences together with 'and then… and then'. They build one long sentence out of **non-finite verbs** and put the only full verb at the very end. You know most of the pieces; here they are together.

**1. Then: the past participle (-ಇ / -ಉ)** for a sequence of actions by the same person: ಎದ್ದು, ಸ್ನಾನ ಮಾಡಿ, ತಿಂಡಿ ತಿಂದು ಹೊರಟೆ 'I got up, bathed, had breakfast and left'. Only the last verb shows tense and person.

**2. While: -ತಾ** (written -ಉತ್ತಾ): ಮಾತಾಡ್ತಾ ಮಾತಾಡ್ತಾ ಹೊತ್ತೇ ಗೊತ್ತಾಗಲಿಲ್ಲ 'we were so busy chatting we lost track of time'; ಡ್ರೈವ್ ಮಾಡ್ತಾ ಫೋನ್ ನೋಡಬೇಡ 'don't look at your phone while driving'.

**3. When, if, even if**: -ಆಗ (ಬಂದಾಗ), -ಅರೆ (ಬಂದ್ರೆ), -ಅರೂ (ಬಂದ್ರೂ) (units 19 and 30).

**4. Because / since: verbal noun + -ಇಂದ**, spoken **-ಓದ್ರಿಂದ**: ಮಳೆ ಬರ್ತಿರೋದ್ರಿಂದ ಟ್ರಿಪ್ ಮುಂದೂಡಿದ್ವಿ 'because it was raining we postponed the trip'; past: ಕೆಲಸ ಬದಲಾಯಿಸಿದ್ರಿಂದ 'since I changed jobs' (written ಬದಲಾಯಿಸಿದ್ದರಿಂದ). In casual speech, just say the reason and add ಅದಕ್ಕೆ or ಹಾಗಾಗಿ.

**5. So that: -ಲಿ + ಅಂತ**: ಎಲ್ಲರಿಗೂ ಸೀಟ್ ಸಿಗಲಿ ಅಂತ ಬೇಗ ಹೋದ್ವಿ 'we went early so that everyone would get a seat'. When the doer is the same, the infinitive is enough: ಬಸ್ ಹಿಡಿಯೋಕೆ ಓಡಿದೆ 'I ran to catch the bus'.

**6. Without: -ಅದೆ** (spoken -ದೇ): ಹೇಳದೆ ಹೋದ 'he left without telling anyone'; the doubled ಹೇಳದೆ ಕೇಳದೆ means 'out of the blue, without warning'.

**7. Since (given that): past relative participle + ಮೇಲೆ**: ನೀನೇ ಹೇಳಿದ ಮೇಲೆ ಇನ್ನೇನು? 'since you said so yourself, what more is there?'

**Between whole sentences**: ಹಾಗಾಗಿ 'so', ಆದ್ರೂ 'even so', ಇಲ್ಲಾಂದ್ರೆ 'otherwise', ಅಷ್ಟೇ ಅಲ್ಲ 'not only that', ಹೇಗೂ 'anyway, since … anyway', ಒಟ್ಟಿನಲ್ಲಿ 'all in all'.

Rule of thumb: one subject doing several things → chain them with -ಇ and finish with a single real verb.

examples.native: ಊಟ ಮಾಡಿ, ಸ್ವಲ್ಪ ಹರಟೆ ಹೊಡೆದು, ಹತ್ತು ಗಂಟೆಗೆ ಮನೆಗೆ ಹೊರಟ್ವಿ.
examples.roman: ūṭa māḍi, svalpa haraṭe hoḍedu, hattu gaṇṭege manege horaṭvi.
examples.en: We ate, chatted for a bit and set off home at ten.
We were chatting so much we lost track of time.
Because it was raining, we postponed the trip.

examples.native: ಎಲ್ಲರಿಗೂ ಸೀಟ್ ಸಿಗಲಿ ಅಂತ ಬೇಗ ಹೋದ್ವಿ.
examples.roman: ellarigū sīṭ sigali anta bēga hōdvi.
examples.en: We went early so that everyone would get a seat.

grammar.title: Switching register mid-conversation
grammar.body:
Real conversations rarely stay in one register. At a family dinner you might speak to your grandmother, an aunt, a cousin and a child within a minute, and Kannada makes you choose every time.

**The two 'you's and their verbs** (unit 1):
ನೀನು → imperative ಬಾ, ಕೂತ್ಕೊ, ತಗೊ; questions ಬರ್ತೀಯಾ?, ಬಂದ್ಯಾ?
ನೀವು → imperative ಬನ್ನಿ, ಕೂತ್ಕೊಳ್ಳಿ, ತಗೊಳ್ಳಿ; questions ಬರ್ತೀರಾ?, ಬಂದ್ರಾ?

**Who gets what in a family**: grandparents, uncles and aunts, in-laws and most elders get **ನೀವು** (in many families parents too); siblings, younger cousins, children and old friends get **ನೀನು**. Elders speak *down* with ನೀನು plus -ಅಪ್ಪ / -ಅಮ್ಮ (ಬಾರಪ್ಪ, ಹೇಳಮ್ಮ), which is affectionate. Talking *about* an elder, use the respectful plural: ಮಾವ ಬಂದ್ರು, ಅಜ್ಜಿ ಮಲಗಿದ್ದಾರೆ, not ಬಂದ / ಮಲಗಿದ್ದಾಳೆ.

**Groups**: ನೀವು / ನೀವೆಲ್ಲ 'you all' with plural verbs; to a group of kids or friends add **-ರೋ** (or -ರೇ to girls): ಬನ್ರೋ, ಹೋಗ್ರೋ 'come on, you lot'.

**Switching on purpose**:
• ನೀನು → ನೀವು with a friend signals sudden coldness or sarcasm: ಆಯ್ತು, ನೀವೇ ದೊಡ್ಡವರು! 'fine, you're the boss!'
• ನೀವು → ನೀನು with a stranger signals anger or contempt; avoid it.
• When someone senior joins the group, switch to ನೀವು forms at once and drop the slang (ಮಗಾ, ಹೋಗೋ).
• When an acquaintance warms up, move from ನೀವು to the friendlier ನೀವು + -ರೀ (ಹೇಳ್ರೀ), and to ನೀನು only when they invite it: ನೀನು ಅಂತ ಕರೀರಿ, ಪರವಾಗಿಲ್ಲ 'call me ನೀನು, it's fine'.

**English as neutral ground**: when people aren't sure which register fits (a new colleague, a flatmate's parent), they often slide into English or use ನೀವು with first names. That's normal in Bengaluru.

examples.en: Ajji, you sit down, I'll serve.

examples.native: ಅಪ್ಪ ಇನ್ನೂ ಆಫೀಸಿಂದ ಬಂದಿಲ್ಲ, ಬಂದ ತಕ್ಷಣ ಫೋನ್ ಮಾಡ್ತಾರೆ.
examples.roman: appa innū āphīsinda bandilla, banda takṣaṇa phōn māḍtāre.
examples.en: Dad isn't back from the office yet, he'll call as soon as he's home.

examples.native: ಆಯ್ತು, ನೀವೇ ದೊಡ್ಡವರು, ನೀವು ಹೇಳಿದ ಹಾಗೇ ಆಗಲಿ!
examples.roman: āytu, nīvē doḍḍavaru, nīvu hēḷida hāgē āgali!
examples.en: Fine, you're the boss, have it your way! (sarcastic, to a friend)

dialogue.title: Deepavali dinner at Ajji's
dialogue.setting: Nikhil comes home from Bengaluru to his grandmother's house in Mysuru for Deepavali. His aunt (Chikkamma) is serving, and his cousin Sneha is planning a trip.

lines.speaker: Ajji
lines.native: ಬಾರಪ್ಪ ನಿಖಿಲ್! ಎಷ್ಟು ದಿನ ಆಯ್ತು ನಿನ್ನ ನೋಡಿ. ಸಣ್ಣಗಾಗಿಬಿಟ್ಟಿದ್ದೀಯ!
lines.roman: bārappa nikhil! eṣṭu dina āytu ninna nōḍi. saṇṇagāgibiṭṭiddīya!
lines.en: Come in, Nikhil! It's been so long since I saw you. You've got so thin!

lines.speaker: Nikhil
lines.native: ಅಜ್ಜಿ, ನೀವು ಪ್ರತಿ ಸಲ ಇದನ್ನೇ ಹೇಳ್ತೀರ! ಆರೋಗ್ಯ ಹೇಗಿದೆ? ಕಾಲು ನೋವು ಕಡಿಮೆ ಆಯ್ತಾ?
lines.roman: ajji, nīvu prati sala idannē hēḷtīra! ārōgya hēgide? kālu nōvu kaḍime āytā?
lines.en: Ajji, you say that every time! How is your health? Is your leg pain better?

lines.speaker: Ajji
lines.native: ದೇವರ ದಯೆ, ಪರವಾಗಿಲ್ಲ. ಅದು ಬಿಡು, ನಿನ್ನ ಮದುವೆ ಯಾವಾಗ? ಒಂದು ಒಳ್ಳೆ ಸಂಬಂಧ ಬಂದಿದೆ...
lines.roman: dēvara daye, paravāgilla. adu biḍu, ninna maduve yāvāga? ondu oḷḷe sambandha bandide...
lines.en: By God's grace, not bad. Forget that, when's your wedding? A good proposal has come...

lines.speaker: Nikhil
lines.native: ಅಯ್ಯೋ ಅಜ್ಜಿ, ಮೊದಲು ಊಟ ಮಾಡೋಣ, ಆಮೇಲೆ ಮಾತಾಡೋಣ. ಚಿಕ್ಕಮ್ಮ, ಹೋಳಿಗೆ ಸೂಪರ್ ಆಗಿದೆ!
lines.roman: ayyō ajji, modalu ūṭa māḍōṇa, āmēle mātāḍōṇa. chikkamma, hōḷige sūpar āgide!
lines.en: Oh Ajji, let's eat first and talk later. Chikkamma, the holige is amazing!

lines.speaker: Chikkamma
lines.native: ಇನ್ನೊಂದು ಹಾಕ್ಲಾ? ಬೆಂಗಳೂರಲ್ಲಿ ಹೇಗೂ ಸರಿಯಾಗಿ ಊಟ ಮಾಡಲ್ಲ ನೀನು.
lines.roman: innondu hāklā? beṅgaḷūralli hēgū sariyāgi ūṭa māḍalla nīnu.
lines.en: Shall I give you another? You don't eat properly in Bengaluru anyway.

lines.speaker: Nikhil
lines.native: ಸಾಕು ಚಿಕ್ಕಮ್ಮ, ಹೊಟ್ಟೆ ತುಂಬಿತು. ಸ್ನೇಹಾ, ಮುಂದಿನ ತಿಂಗಳ ಟ್ರಿಪ್ ಪ್ಲಾನ್ ಏನಾಯ್ತು?
lines.roman: sāku chikkamma, hoṭṭe tumbitu. snēhā, mundina tiṅgaḷa ṭrip plān ēnāytu?
lines.en: That's enough, Chikkamma, I'm full. Sneha, what happened to next month's trip plan?

lines.speaker: Sneha
lines.native: ನಾನು ಗೋಕರ್ಣ ಅಂತೀನಿ, ಬೀಚ್, ಸೂರ್ಯಾಸ್ತ... ಆದ್ರೆ ಕಾವ್ಯ ಕೊಡಗೇ ಬೇಕು ಅಂತ ಹಠ ಮಾಡ್ತಿದ್ದಾಳೆ.
lines.roman: nānu gōkarṇa antīni, bīch, sūryāsta... ādre kāvya koḍagē bēku anta haṭha māḍtiddāḷe.
lines.en: I say Gokarna, the beach, the sunset... but Kavya is insisting it has to be Kodagu.

lines.speaker: Nikhil
lines.native: ಕೊಡಗು ಆದ್ರೆ ಹೋಂಸ್ಟೇ ಸಿಗುತ್ತೆ, ಮಳೆ ಇದ್ರೂ ಜಲಪಾತ ನೋಡ್ಬಹುದು. ಗೋಕರ್ಣಕ್ಕೆ ಘಾಟ್ ದಾರಿ, ಎಂಟು ಗಂಟೆ ಆಗುತ್ತೆ.
lines.roman: koḍagu ādre hōmsṭē sigutte, maḷe idrū jalapāta nōḍbahudu. gōkarṇakke ghāṭ dāri, eṇṭu gaṇṭe āgutte.
lines.en: In Kodagu we'd get a homestay, and even if it rains we can see the waterfalls. Gokarna is all ghat roads, it takes eight hours.

lines.speaker: Sneha
lines.native: ಓಹೋ, ನೀನೂ ಅವಳ ಕಡೆನಾ? ಸರಿ, ವೋಟ್ ಮಾಡೋಣ. ಇಲ್ಲಾಂದ್ರೆ ಈ ಜಗಳ ಮುಗಿಯಲ್ಲ.
lines.roman: ōhō, nīnū avaḷa kaḍenā? sari, vōṭ māḍōṇa. illāndre ī jagaḷa mugiyalla.
lines.en: Oho, you're on her side too? Fine, let's vote. Otherwise this fight will never end.

lines.speaker: Nikhil
lines.native: ಏನಿಲ್ಲ ಅಜ್ಜಿ, ಟ್ರಿಪ್ ಬಗ್ಗೆ ಮಾತುಕತೆ. ನೀವೂ ಬರ್ತೀರಾ ನಮ್ಜೊತೆ ಕೊಡಗಿಗೆ?
lines.roman: ēnilla ajji, ṭrip bagge mātukate. nīvū bartīrā namjote koḍagige?
lines.en: Nothing, Ajji, we're just discussing the trip. Will you come with us to Kodagu?

lines.speaker: Ajji
lines.native: ನಾನಾ? ಹೋಗ್ರೋ! ನಿಮ್ಮ ವಯಸ್ಸಲ್ಲಿ ನಾನು ಬೆಟ್ಟ ಎಲ್ಲಾ ನಡ್ಕೊಂಡೇ ಹತ್ತುತ್ತಿದ್ದೆ!
lines.roman: nānā? hōgrō! nimma vayassalli nānu beṭṭa ellā naḍkoṇḍē hattuttidde!
lines.en: Me? Go on with you! At your age I used to climb every hill on foot!

lines.speaker: Sneha
lines.native: ಸರಿ, ರಾಜಿ ಆಗೋಣ: ಈ ಸಲ ಕೊಡಗು, ಡಿಸೆಂಬರ್‌ನಲ್ಲಿ ಗೋಕರ್ಣ. ಆದ್ರೆ ಬಜೆಟ್ ಎಲ್ಲಾ ನಿಖಿಲ್ ನೋಡ್ಕೊಳ್ತಾನೆ!
lines.roman: sari, rāji āgōṇa: ī sala koḍagu, ḍisembarnalli gōkarṇa. ādre bajeṭ ellā nikhil nōḍkoḷtāne!
lines.en: OK, let's compromise: Kodagu this time, Gokarna in December. But Nikhil handles the whole budget!

lines.speaker: Nikhil
lines.native: ಹೋಗ್ಲಿ, ಹಾಗೇ ಆಗಲಿ. ಅಜ್ಜಿ, ನೋಡಿ, ನಿಮ್ಮ ಮೊಮ್ಮಗಳು ನನ್ನನ್ನ ಹೇಗೆ ಬಳಸ್ಕೊಳ್ತಿದ್ದಾಳೆ!
lines.roman: hōgli, hāgē āgali. ajji, nōḍi, nimma mommagaḷu nannanna hēge baḷaskoḷtiddāḷe!
lines.en: Fine, so be it. Ajji, look how your granddaughter is using me!

culture:
Family gatherings in Karnataka revolve around food and questions. Expect elders to comment on your weight (ಸಣ್ಣಗಾಗಿದ್ದೀಯ 'you've got thin' is affection, not criticism), ask about your job and salary, and bring up marriage (ಒಳ್ಳೆ ಸಂಬಂಧ 'a good match'). The polite way out is humour and food: ಮೊದಲು ಊಟ ಮಾಡೋಣ. Greet elders first, with ನಮಸ್ಕಾರ or by touching their feet at festivals, ask ಆರೋಗ್ಯ ಹೇಗಿದೆ?, and keep ನೀವು with them however close you are. Hosts will serve you again and again (ಇನ್ನೊಂದು ಹಾಕ್ಲಾ?); refuse with ಸಾಕು, ಹೊಟ್ಟೆ ತುಂಬಿತು and a hand over your banana leaf.

Among friends and cousins, plans get made noisily: in a WhatsApp group, by vote, with someone sulking (ಮುನಿಸ್ಕೊಂಡಿದ್ದಾಳೆ) until a ರಾಜಿ is found. Favourite weekend trips from Bengaluru and Mysuru are Kodagu and Chikkamagaluru for homestays and coffee estates, Gokarna and Udupi for beaches and temples, Hampi for ruins, and Jog Falls in the monsoon. If you can switch smoothly from ನೀವು with Ajji to ನೀನು with your cousin to ಬನ್ರೋ for the whole gang, you're no longer a learner, you're part of the family.

lessons.title: Catching up with an old friend

tip.title: One long sentence: -ಇ … -ಇ … verb
tip.body:
- Chain actions with the past participle: ಕಾಲೇಜು **ಮುಗಿಸಿ**, ಪುಣೆಗೆ **ಹೋಗಿ**, ಈಗ ವಾಪಸ್ ಬಂದಿದ್ದೀನಿ. Only the last verb has tense.
- While: **-ತಾ**: ಮಾತಾಡ್ತಾ ಮಾತಾಡ್ತಾ.
- Because: **-ಓದ್ರಿಂದ / -ಇದ್ರಿಂದ**: ಬದಲಾಯಿಸಿದ್ರಿಂದ.
- Without: **-ಅದೆ**: ಹೇಳದೆ. So that: **-ಲಿ ಅಂತ**.

tip.title: ನೀವು for Ajji, ನೀನು for your cousin
tip.body:
- Elders (grandparents, uncles, aunts, in-laws): **ನೀವು** + ಬನ್ನಿ, ಮಾಡಿ, -ತೀರಾ?
- Siblings, younger cousins, kids: **ನೀನು** + ಬಾ, ಮಾಡು, -ತೀಯಾ?
- Talking *about* an elder: plural verb: ಮಾವ **ಬಂದ್ರು**, ಚಿಕ್ಕಪ್ಪ **ಹೇಗಿದ್ದಾರೆ**?
- A group: **ಬನ್ರೋ**. Drop slang when an elder joins.
tip.pattern: ಅಜ್ಜಿ, ನೀವು … ಬನ್ನಿ · ತಮ್ಮ, ನೀನು … ಬಾ
